::: {#lem-dfs-one-call}
#### Depth-first search calls itself once on each vertex

Let $G$ be a connected (@def-connected) graph with no parallel edges (@def-parallel-edges),
given by an adjacency list (@def-adjacency-list), and let $s$ be a vertex of $G$.
Then `dfs(G, s)` (@def-dfs) makes exactly one call `dfs(G, u)` on each vertex $u$ of $G$,
and for $u \ne s$ that call is made by a call `dfs(G, v)` with $v$ adjacent (@def-adjacent) to $u$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

**At most one call.**
Apart from the first call, a call `dfs(G, u)` is made only when $u$ is not marked,
and every call `dfs(G, u)` marks $u$ before it makes any other call.
Marks are never removed, so after the first call on $u$, $u$ stays marked, and no later call on $u$ is made.

**At least one call.**
Since $G$ is connected, there is a walk (@def-walk) from $s$ to every vertex,
so @thm-dfs-reachable says that `dfs(G, s)` marks every vertex.
A vertex is marked only by a call on it, so there is a call on every vertex.

**Who makes the call.**
For $u \ne s$, the call on $u$ is not the first call,
so it is made by a call `dfs(G, v)` while it goes through the list of $v$,
and $u$ is in that list, so $u$ is adjacent to $v$.

:::

:::
